question: Four statements about the setting are attributed to you in the research record with no recorded words, and nothing in your notes or the research backs them: (1) shrine approaches have 1, 3 or 7 arches because those numbers carry power, seven most of all, and a few named great sites have long donated rows (0220; your 2026-09-29 words back arches at ordinary shrines, not the counts); (2) only a merchant family the daimyo has granted the right may have a walled, gated compound; wealth cannot buy one (0155); (3) the setting is more attentive to its peasantry than its historical models, which is why a city gets a generous count (0185); (4) Hirameki stood unwalled and was walled in haste during the Lion/Crane war, which excuses its shortfall in housing (0002).
